beats.text: You think attractive people are mean. Watch this.
Four hundred people. Looks and kindness, totally random. No link at all.
Now drop everyone you'd never date. Not hot enough, and not kind enough.
Look who's left. The hotter, the meaner!
Nobody changed. Only your filter did. It's called Berkson's paradox. And it's why

sources: Berkson (1946), Limitations of the application of fourfold table analysis to hospital data, Biometrics Bulletin 2(3), 47–53.
Ellenberg (2014), How Not to Be Wrong.
Simulation: 400 people, looks and kindness independent (r = −0.01); keeping looks + kindness > 1 leaves 209 people with r = −0.54.
